result.markdown: --- title: "[extract_time()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Extract the times from an event-time vector. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_event_time.py#L787-L821){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python extract_time(x) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A port of etd's `extract_time()`. Like etd, the shape depends on the data: a 1-D array when no element is interval-censored, otherwise a 2-D array with columns `time` and `time_max`, where `time_max` is missing (`nan`) for elements that aren't interval-censored. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [x]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : An `EventTime` vector. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [numpy.ndarray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A 1-D float array of times, or a 2-D float array of shape `(n, 2)` holding `time` and `time_max` when any element is interval-censored. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#9c84478e .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw x = gw.event_time(time=[7, 5, 2], status=["e", "r", "i"], time_max=[None, None, 4]) gw.extract_time(x) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` array([[ 7., nan], [ 5., nan], [ 2., 4.]]) ``` ::: ::: Without intervals, the result is 1-D: ::: {#0a2b1f02 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} gw.extract_time(x[0:2]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` array([7., 5.]) ``` ::: :::
